notable_absence.finding: Unlike every other statement page in this batch, EXECUTE has no Prerequisites/privilege table at all. Its Prerequisites section covers only query-context matching ('To execute a prepared statement, the query context must be the same as it was when the prepared statement was created') - there is no textual evidence for what privilege, if any, governs running a prepared statement (presumably inherited from whatever privileges the underlying prepared statement required, but the page never says so).

cross_product_finding: This is not the transaction-statement family this round was told to watch for, but it is the same shape of cross-product link: EXECUTE's Related section links directly and by name to two Java SDK pages ('Prepared Statements for Query Optimization' and 'Parameterized Queries', ../../../java-sdk/current/...). This is page-attested textual evidence of a Capella N1QL -> Java SDK cross-reference, distinct from and unrelated to sdk:distributed-transaction (no transaction content on this page at all).
